body:
A single certification used to be enough to get an IT job. It no longer is. Every serious role today expects a stack of technologies, and that is exactly why the **combo offer** at IT Security Nepal is so relevant for career builders in 2026. Training centers everywhere advertise individual courses, but what actually moves a career forward is a connected bundle of credentials, learned together, priced so that building that stack does not ruin your savings. This article explains why the bundled-training model fits the way today’s IT careers are really built.

### Today’s IT Careers Are Built on Stacks, Not Single Skills
Open any job posting for a system administrator, DevOps engineer, or cloud operations role and the pattern is obvious: the requirement list is never one technology. It is Linux plus automation, or networking plus containers, or security plus administration. Employers are not asking for extras; they are describing the way modern infrastructure actually works. Servers run an operating system, connect through a network, and get managed through automation, and the person who understands all three is the engineer, not the ticket-closer.

That means career builders need a portfolio of interrelated skills, not a collection of disconnected certificates. The more those skills are taught as one story, the faster they become usable in the real world.

### What Exactly Is a Combo Offer?
A combo offer is simply two professional courses bundled into one enrollment at a single combined price. At IT Security Nepal the current [combo offer package](/dashain-offer-it-security-nepal/) works exactly this way: RHCSA plus RHCE, RHCSA plus DevOps, RHCSA plus CCNA, or DevOps plus CCNA, each taught as a continuous track instead of two unrelated enrollments.

The value is not just the discount. Because the courses are delivered back to back, the second course builds directly on the first. System administration reinforces what automation depends on, and networking skills make container troubleshooting make sense. You study once, in one mindset, and the two credentials reinforce each other instead of fighting for attention.

### The Real Advantages of Bundled Training
- **Faster career positioning.** Two linked certifications take less total time than booking the same courses months apart. Momentum matters when you are competing with your own batch of job seekers.
- **Lower total cost.** Bundled pricing beats paying for each course separately, and during a festival window the saving is even larger. Your money goes further toward certification.
- **Stronger interviews.** A candidate who can talk about administration and its next layer immediately answers the follow-up questions that derail single-credential applicants.
- **Remote-job readiness.** International employers hiring Nepali engineers look for breadth plus depth, which is precisely what a connected combo demonstrates.
- **Less friction to start.** One enrollment, one timeline, one goal. You remove the classic trap of finishing a course and never enrolling in the next one.
### Why Combo Offer Training Matters in Nepal Right Now
There is one more advantage worth naming: momentum. Career changes rarely fail because of talent; they fail because the plan stalls between steps. A bundle keeps the study going while motivation is high, carries your progress into the second credential, and delivers the finished package to your resume while the topic still feels fresh.

The remote hiring wave has made Nepal one of the most active markets for international IT talent, but it has also raised the bar. Global teams want engineers who come in ready to work across a small slice of the whole stack, because training remote juniors in multiple technologies is expensive for them. A combo offer is your answer to that bar: it proves you have already invested in the pair, not in a single subject.

For freshers, the timing benefit is equally real. The job market rewards speed, and a bundle lets you reach employable strength in a few months instead of spreading two courses across a year. For working professionals, it offers a clean upgrade path: pick the second credential that extends what you already do, and move into a higher bracket without a gap between trainings.

### Pricing That Fits the Season
The realistic barrier to stacking credentials is usually cost, and that is where bundled pricing changes behavior. Training a student for two professional certifications in Nepal typically requires months of fees; a festival-time [Dashain package in Nepal](/dashain-offer-it-security-nepal/) collapses that into a single accessible amount. Two popular stacks sit at NPR 25,000 and the advanced pairs at NPR 30,000, which is the kind of price point that lets a serious student say yes and start in the same week.

### Combo Offers That Match Real Job Demands
Not every pair fits every person, so the current packages are built around real roles rather than random combinations:

- **RHCSA + RHCE** matches the classic path to senior Linux administration, from [Red Hat System Administration I](/red-hat-system-administration/) through automation with [RHCE (RH294)](/red-hat-certified-system-engineer/).
- **RHCSA + DevOps** targets cloud and automation careers, where system grounding supports the [DevOps training track](/devops/) and its pipelines, containers, and orchestration.
- **RHCSA + CCNA** builds the full infrastructure profile of a modern admin, connecting user and storage management with routing and switching fundamentals.
- **DevOps + CCNA** suits engineers who want automation fluency plus a solid networking foundation, the profile infrastructure teams hire for.
### How to Choose the Right Combo Offer for Your Goals
Start with the job title you actually want, then pick the pair underneath it. Want to become a Red Hat administrator? RHCSA plus RHCE is your direct line. Cloud and DevOps as a goal? Pair RHCSA with [DevOps](/devops/). Fresher building the broadest possible foundation? RHCSA plus CCNA gives you servers and networks together. Already experienced, and want to round out automation and networking? DevOps plus CCNA extends what you can already do.

Whichever pair you choose, remember that the point of a package is not the certificate count. It is the connected thinking it produces between two layers of technology, which is the exact skill employers pay for.

### The Smartest Career Decision This Season
A **combo offer** is a decision about your professional baseline, not just your next course. It compresses the time to employability, stretches your training budget, and produces a candidate profile that matches what today’s job postings actually describe. During the Dashain window you can claim that advantage at a price designed for it.

If you are building your IT career and want to move faster, call IT Security Nepal at **(+977) 985-1165508** or **(+977) 981-8253111**, or write to us through the [contact page](/contact/) and ask about the current combo offer. Check the full details on our [Dashain combo packages](/dashain-offer-it-security-nepal/) page and reserve your seat before the batch closes.

body:
**Linux training in Nepal** has never been more valuable. Almost every server, every cloud instance, and every containerized application you touch runs on Linux, yet very few institutes teach it the way serious employers expect. The **Linux Bootcamp at IT Security Nepal** changes that. It runs **every Monday to Friday from 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM** and it covers everything: from your very first command to system administration, scripting, security, troubleshooting — and it doubles as **RHCSA (Red Hat Certified System Administrator)** preparation. One focused batch, one complete skill set, and a schedule designed to fit students, job seekers, and working professionals.

- [What Does “Covers All” Actually Include?](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#What_Does_%E2%80%9CCovers_All%E2%80%9D_Actually_Include)[1. Linux Fundamentals](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#1_Linux_Fundamentals) | [2. System Administration](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#2_System_Administration) | [3. Networking and DNS](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#3_Networking_and_DNS) | [4. Storage and Filesystems](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#4_Storage_and_Filesystems) | [5. Scripting and Automation](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#5_Scripting_and_Automation) | [6. Security and SELinux](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#6_Security_and_SELinux) | [7. Troubleshooting and Real-World Scenarios](/linux-bootcamp-nepal/#7_Troubleshooting_and_Real-World_Scenarios)
### Why Linux Skills Matter Now More Than Ever
Linux powers the modern IT world. Web servers, databases, cloud platforms like AWS and Azure, Kubernetes containers, network devices, and even most security tools run on top of it. Global companies increasingly hire remote system administrators, cloud engineers, and DevOps specialists, and that talent pool is still small. That is exactly why a structured **linux bootcamp** is one of the smartest investments a fresher can make in 2026.

Unlike a few YouTube tutorials, a proper bootcamp forces you to spend real hours on the terminal every single day. You stop memorizing commands and start understanding systems. That daily repetition is what turns a beginner into someone employers trust to manage a production server.

### What Is the Linux Bootcamp at IT Security Nepal?
The **Linux bootcamp** at IT Security Nepal is a complete, hands-on program delivered in our classroom at New Baneshwor, Kathmandu. The batch runs **Monday to Friday, 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM**, which gives you twenty hours of guided, instructor-led practice every week. It is built for complete beginners, so you do not need prior command-line experience or an IT degree to join.

Every session is practical. You work on real systems, configure services, break things on purpose, and fix them. Mentors with industry experience guide you at every step, and you keep lifetime access to support and resources even after the batch finishes.

### Who Is This Linux Course For?
This program is designed for a wide range of learners:

- **Fresh graduates and students** who want a job-ready skill before entering the IT market.
- **IT support professionals** moving up from hardware and helpdesk roles into system administration.
- **Working professionals** who need skills for cloud, DevOps, or security roles.
- **Career switchers** who want a practical, high-demand technical skill without spending years in college.
- **Anyone planning a security- or cloud-aligned certification** and wants structured, guided preparation.
The 1 PM to 5 PM weeknight-friendly schedule means you can attend without abandoning a day job or other classes, which makes it one of the most practical **linux classes in Kathmandu** for busy people.

### What Does “Covers All” Actually Include?
When we say this bootcamp covers everything, we mean the complete journey from zero to confident administrator. The curriculum is divided into clear modules:

#### 1. Linux Fundamentals
- Installing and configuring distributions (RHEL, Ubuntu, Debian).
- The file system hierarchy, navigation, and essential commands.
- User permissions, ownership, and secure file handling.
#### 2. System Administration
- User and group administration.
- Package management with apt, yum, and dnf.
- Managing services, daemons, and boot processes.
#### 3. Networking and DNS
- Configuring network interfaces and hostnames.
- Firewalls, services, DNS resolution, and remote access with SSH.
- Basic network troubleshooting from the command line.
#### 4. Storage and Filesystems
- Partitions, LVM, filesystem creation, and mounting.
- Disk usage, quotas, and storage troubleshooting.
#### 5. Scripting and Automation
- Shell scripting with Bash.
- Automating tasks with cron and systemd timers.
- Logging, monitoring, and performance tuning.
#### 6. Security and SELinux
- User security, permissions hardening, and encryption.
- SELinux and AppArmor basics.
- Hardening servers against common attacks.
#### 7. Troubleshooting and Real-World Scenarios
- Diagnosing slow systems and failed services.
- Backup and recovery strategies.
- Live troubleshooting drills that mirror real jobs.
By the end of the batch you will have configured, secured, and automated full production-style systems from scratch — not just passed quizzes.

### Monday to Friday, 1 PM to 5 PM: A Schedule That Works
Most people fail to learn Linux not because it is hard, but because they study inconsistently. This bootcamp removes that risk with a fixed daily routine. From **1:00 PM to 5:00 PM every Monday to Friday**, you sit down, open a terminal, and get guided practice. Twenty hours a week of focused terminal time is more than most self-taught students cover in two months.

The consistent schedule also means you can plan your internship, part-time work, or college classes around it. And because the batch is instructor-led, you never get stuck for days on a single error — a mentor is right there to unblock you.

### A Typical Day in the Bootcamp
Wondering what four hours of daily training actually looks like? Each session follows a proven flow that keeps you building skill, not just watching:

- **Recap and warm-up (30 minutes):** a quick review of the previous day’s tasks and a short drill to lock in the commands.
- **Concept session (60 minutes):** the instructor demonstrates a topic end-to-end on a real system, explaining why, not just how.
- **Hands-on lab (120 minutes):** you work the same scenario yourself. This is where the real learning happens — your machine, your mistakes, your fixes.
- **Mock scenario and review (30 minutes):** a mini tasks-based drill that mirrors exam-style and work-style problems, followed by feedback.
That rhythm — small concept, big lab, immediate feedback — is the same structure used in high-quality professional training worldwide, and it is exactly why students leave the batch able to work independently on a live command line.

### Guided Bootcamp vs Free Self-Study
A valid question: why pay for a bootcamp when YouTube is free? The honest answer is that free resources teach you commands, while a guided bootcamp teaches you judgment. Here is the difference in practice:

- **Structure.** Self-study means choosing what to learn every day; the bootcamp hands you a tested sequence so you never waste weeks on trivia.
- **Stuck-time.** Alone, one cryptic error can eat an entire weekend. Here, a mentor solves the blocker in minutes.
- **Lab access.** Free tutorials rarely give you real systems to break and rebuild; every bootcamp session is a real lab.
- **Accountability.** Showing up daily at 1 PM keeps you progressing even on low-motivation days.
- **Certification direction.** The batch points your study toward recognized exams, so your effort converts into credentials employers recognize.
Self-study works for a lucky few. A daily guided program works for almost everyone — which is precisely why so many job seekers choose the structured path.

### Which Certifications Does the Bootcamp Prepare You For?
Completing this **Linux training in Nepal** naturally prepares you for globally recognized certifications. If you want a vendor-neutral credential, the bootcamp’s fundamentals, security, and scripting modules map directly to [CompTIA Linux+ (XK0-005)](/comptia-linux/). If your goal is enterprise Red Hat skills, the system administration and SELinux content is the ideal foundation for our [Red Hat System Administration I (RH124)](/red-hat-system-administration/) course and the RHCSA track — the same path our [RHCSA certification guide](/rhcsa-certification-guide/) explains in detail.

Certifications matter, but the bootcamp’s real goal is the skill underneath. A certified engineer who cannot fix a broken system is useless; a bootcamp graduate who has rebuilt broken systems daily is valuable on day one.

### RHCSA Included: Built-In Red Hat Exam Preparation
If you are aiming for the **RHCSA (EX200)** exam, this bootcamp is where preparation must begin. RHCSA is Red Hat’s performance-based certification: instead of multiple-choice questions, you sit at a real RHEL system and perform hands-on tasks — configuring users, managing storage, securing services, and troubleshooting. That is precisely the style of practice the bootcamp runs daily.

Every module supports the official RHCSA exam objectives:

- **Essential tools and shell skills** that form the exam’s foundation.
- **Operating running systems**: boot, init, services, logs, and systemd.
- **Local storage**: partitions, LVM, filesystems, and mounts.
- **User and group administration** with correct permissions and ownership.
- **Security, firewall, and SELinux basics** — a domain many self-taught candidates fail.
After the bootcamp, students typically continue into our [Red Hat System Administration II (RH134)](/red-hat-system-administration-ii/) training and then sit the exam, supported by instructors every step of the way. You can read exactly what the exam costs and how long it takes in our [complete RHCSA guide](/rhcsa-certification-guide/), but the short version is: guided lab practice and timed mock tasks dramatically shorten the road to passing. Our students enjoy a proven track record of passing Red Hat exams, and the bootcamp’s daily hands-on format is the reason.

### Linux Training in Nepal: Why Choose IT Security Nepal
IT Security Nepal is a **Red Hat authorized training partner with over 15 years of experience** and more than 1,580 successfully certified students. That combination matters:

- **Industry-experienced instructors** who work in the field, not just in theory.
- **Hands-on labs and real-world scenarios** in every session.
- **Lifetime support** — you can come back with questions even after the batch.
- **Career guidance** to help you turn the skill into a job.
- **Multiple training modes**: classroom, live virtual, one-on-one, and corporate training.
Students regularly move from these batches into roles as system administrators and network engineers, often with companies hiring for remote work. If you are wondering whether **Linux training in Nepal** will pay off, talk to any recent graduate — almost all of them will tell you the terminal skills came first, and the job offers followed.

### Career Paths After the Bootcamp
A completed bootcamp opens doors across IT. Typical next roles include junior system administrator, systems engineer, DevOps associate, cloud operations support, and data center technician. From there, adding our [Red Hat System Administration II (RH134)](/red-hat-system-administration-ii/) training or a [cybersecurity career roadmap](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/) can push you toward senior engineering and security roles with substantially higher pay.

The fastest career path in Nepal’s job market right now is: learn Linux properly, combine it with cloud or security skills, and position yourself for remote and international roles. This bootcamp is step one of that path.

### How to Enroll in the Bootcamp
Enrolling is simple. Batches are limited so that every student gets personal attention, and seats fill quickly once a batch is announced. Here is what to do:

- Check the full [course list](/course/) to compare the bootcamp with other programs.
- Call or message us at **(+977) 981-8253111** or **(+977) 985-1165508**.
- Visit our [contact page](/contact/) to book a free career counseling session.

title: RHCSA Certification Guide: How to Pass & What It Costs
excerpt: The RHCSA certification is the most respected entry credential in the Red Hat Linux world. Short for Red Hat Certified System Administrator, it proves you can actually administer a Red Hat Enterprise…
body:
The **RHCSA certification** is the most respected entry credential in the Red Hat Linux world. Short for Red Hat Certified System Administrator, it proves you can actually administer a Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) system in a real environment. If you want a career as a Linux system administrator or a future as a Red Hat engineer, RHCSA is where every serious path begins. This guide explains the exam, the cost, how long it takes to study, and exactly how to pass it.

### What Is the RHCSA Certification?
RHCSA is a performance-based exam from Red Hat. Unlike multiple-choice tests, you sit at a real RHEL system and complete hands-on tasks: configuring users, managing storage, securing services, and troubleshooting. You are not asked to recall facts; you are asked to do the job. That is why employers trust it so much. A candidate who holds RHCSA has proven they can work on the command line under pressure.

The certification is vendor-specific, which means it focuses on Red Hat Enterprise Linux. In practice, the skills you learn transfer cleanly to other enterprise Linux distributions, making RHCSA one of the most versatile system-level certifications available.

### Who Should Take the RHCSA?
RHCSA suits a wide range of people:

- IT support professionals moving toward system administration.
- Students building the first credential of a Linux career.
- Network security specialists who need deeper operating system skills.
- Anyone preparing for the more advanced RHCE certification.
You do not need an IT degree, but you should be comfortable with basic computing and willing to spend real time on the command line.

### What Does the RHCSA Exam Cover?
The exam tests practical tasks organized around core exam domains:

- Understanding and using essential Linux tools.
- Operating running systems: boot, init, services, and logs.
- Managing local storage: partitions, LVM, filesystems, and mounts.
- Creating and configuring file systems and networking.
- Administering users, groups, passwords, and permissions.
- Deploying, monitoring, and troubleshooting services.
- Managing security, firewall rules, and SELinux basics.
The exact task list changes over time, so always check the current Red Hat exam objectives for your exam code before booking.

### RHCSA Cost in Nepal: What You Will Actually Pay
Budgeting accurately matters, so here is the real breakdown for candidates in Nepal. The official RHCSA exam fee is around **$175 USD**. However, due to local rules and regulations, an additional **13% tax (VAT)** plus bank and processing charges are applied when you purchase the exam voucher. Adding these together, your **total approximate cost for certification will be NPR 30,000 to 35,000**, depending on the exact exchange rate and bank charges on the day you pay.

- **Exam voucher:** approximately $175 USD.
- **Additional tax:** 13% VAT charged on the exam fee.
- **Bank and processing charges:** applied on the international payment.
- **Estimated total in Nepal:** NPR 30,000 to 35,000.
The certification is valid for three years before renewal is required. On top of the exam fee, set aside a realistic budget for training if you choose to prepare with a guided course, because a structured program saves you months of wandering, and most successful candidates budget for guided lab time plus realistic mock tasks rather than paying only the exam fee.

### How Long Does It Take to Prepare?
With consistent study, most motivated beginners reach exam readiness in two to four months. A realistic weekly plan looks like this:

- **Week 1-2:** Set up a RHEL virtual machine and learn the shell, files, and basic commands.
- **Week 3-6:** Work through the exam domains one by one, practising each task many times.
- **Week 7-10:** Full realistic practice exams from scratch, timed, without notes.
- **Week 11-12:** Fix weaknesses, repeat practice exams, and book the real exam.
Consistency beats marathon sessions. Thirty to sixty focused minutes daily will take you further than weekend cramming.

### The Best Way to Study for RHCSA
Passing RHCSA is about hands-on repetition. These methods work best:

- Install RHEL on a virtual machine and break it on purpose, then fix it.
- Work through the official Red Hat exam objectives checklist task by task.
- Use practice exams and do them from a blank system, exactly like exam day.
- Take a structured course if you need pacing, especially one with labs included.
- Join Linux communities and explain what you learn to others; it deeply reinforces the skill.
Timed practice is essential. On exam day you must work quickly, and speed only comes from repetition.

### Prepare for RHCSA with IT Security Nepal
Studying alone is possible, but guided training dramatically shortens the road to certification. At IT Security Nepal, our professional instructors prepare you for real-world industry challenges, not just theory. Our [Red Hat System Administration II (RH134)](/red-hat-system-administration-ii/) course is built around hands-on labs and realistic exam scenarios, and we actively support your **exam preparation** every step of the way: structured lab practice, timed mock tasks, and one-on-one instructor guidance so you walk into the exam ready. Whether you are a student, a working professional, or a fresh graduate, our Red Hat training is designed to help you pass and build a real career in Linux system administration.

Contact IT Security Nepal to check the current batch schedule and fees, and find out how our instructors can help with your specific RHCSA exam preparation plan.

### RHCSA vs RHCE: The Right Order
Red Hat certification has a clear ladder. RHCSA proves system administration fundamentals. The Red Hat Certified Engineer (RHCE) exam builds on RHCSA and covers advanced automation with Ansible and deeper service configuration. Most employers expect RHCSA first, and holding it is usually a prerequisite for RHCE courses. If a career in system engineering appeals to you, see our guide on [why becoming a Red Hat certified system engineer](/why-become-red-hat-certified-system-engineer/) is a strong career move.

### RHCSA Salary Potential and Career Path
RHCSA holders typically command higher salaries than general IT support roles because the certification signals real, tested skill. Common job titles after RHCSA include junior Linux administrator, system administrator, DevOps associate, and cloud operations support. From there, RHCE opens doors to senior engineering and automation roles. In markets such as Nepal, Red Hat skills are especially valuable because global companies frequently hire Nepali professionals for remote Linux and cloud work.

### Common RHCSA Mistakes to Avoid
- Watching video courses without touching a terminal.
- Skipping timed practice exams until the week before the test.
- Ignoring SELinux, which appears in real exam tasks.
- Memorizing commands without understanding when to apply them.
- Giving up after one failed attempt instead of booking a retake.
### FAQ
- **Is RHCSA worth it for a beginner?** Yes. It is the best first credential for anyone serious about a Linux system administration career.
- **Can I pass RHCSA without a Red Hat course?** Regularly. Self-study with labs and practice exams is a well-trodden path.
- **What is the RHCE exam?** The advanced Red Hat Certified Engineer exam, which assumes RHCSA knowledge and focuses on automation.
- **How long is RHCSA valid?** Three years, after which Red Hat requires re-certification.
### Conclusion
The RHCSA certification is your best, most credible starting point into Linux administration and the Red Hat ecosystem. Set up a lab, work through the official objectives, and practise realistic timed exams until you can complete tasks without notes. The effort is substantial, but the certification is respected exactly because passing it is hard. If you are ready, start your RHCSA journey now.

title: How to Start a Cybersecurity Career in 2026: Full Roadmap
excerpt: Are you wondering how to start a cybersecurity career in 2026? You are not alone. Cybersecurity has become one of the fastest-growing fields in IT, with more open roles than qualified professionals…
body:
Are you wondering how to start a **cybersecurity career** in 2026? You are not alone. Cybersecurity has become one of the fastest-growing fields in IT, with more open roles than qualified professionals to fill them. If you are willing to learn, practice, and earn the right certifications, this field offers a clear path to a high-paying, stable, and genuinely meaningful job. This guide walks you through the entire process, from first skills to first job, step by step.

- [How to Start a Cybersecurity Career: Step-by-Step](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#How_to_Start_a_Cybersecurity_Career_Step-by-Step)[Step 1: Choose one starting point](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_1_Choose_one_starting_point) | [Step 2: Learn the fundamentals hands-on](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_2_Learn_the_fundamentals_hands-on) | [Step 3: Earn your first certification](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_3_Earn_your_first_certification) | [Step 4: Build a visible portfolio](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_4_Build_a_visible_portfolio) | [Step 5: Apply for the entry role](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_5_Apply_for_the_entry_role) | [Step 6: Specialize after experience](/how-to-start-a-cybersecurity-career/#Step_6_Specialize_after_experience)
### Why Cybersecurity Jobs Are Booming in 2026
Every company now runs on digital systems, which means every company faces cyber threats. Ransomware attacks, data breaches, phishing campaigns, and insider threats are no longer rare events. They are everyday risks. As a result, organizations are hiring specialists to protect their networks, systems, and data. The global security talent shortage continues to widen, and employers now compete for candidates who hold even entry-level cybersecurity certifications.

This demand is not limited to big corporations. Banks, hospitals, government agencies, schools, and small businesses all need security professionals. For job seekers, this means less reliance on a traditional four-year degree and more emphasis on practical skills, hands-on labs, and recognized certifications.

### Understanding the Cybersecurity Career Path
A common misconception is that you need to be a “hacker” to enter this industry. In reality, the modern cybersecurity career path splits into two main camps: **offensive security** (red teams, penetration testers, ethical hackers) and **defensive security** (blue teams, SOC analysts, incident responders). Most professionals start on the defensive side because it has more entry-level roles.

Beyond these two camps, you will find specialties such as security architecture, governance and compliance, cloud security, application security, and security engineering. You do not need to choose your final specialty today. Instead, build a strong foundation first, then let experience guide your specialization.

### Core Skills Every Cybersecurity Professional Needs
Before you apply for a single job, focus on building these foundational skills. They appear again and again in cybersecurity job descriptions:

- **Networking fundamentals:** IP addressing, TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls, VPNs, and how data flows across a network.
- **Operating systems:** Comfort with Windows and Linux. A strong Linux foundation is especially valuable.
- **System administration:** Managing users, permissions, patches, and logging so you understand what “normal” looks like.
- **Security basics:** Confidentiality, integrity, and availability (the CIA triad), authentication, authorization, and risk.
- **Common threats:** Phishing, malware, ransomware, SQL injection, and social engineering attacks.
- **Tools:** Wireshark, Nmap, Metasploit, Burp Suite, and SIEM platforms such as Splunk.
- **Soft skills:** Clear writing, incident communication, curiosity, and ethical judgment.
If you are starting from zero and feel overwhelmed, remember that you only need to be consistent. Thirty minutes of daily practice beats weekend cramming.

### Entry-Level Cybersecurity Jobs to Start With
The best way to enter a cybersecurity career is through a role that builds security experience while paying you to learn. Strong starting points include:

- **Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst** — monitors alerts, triages incidents, and analyzes logs.
- **IT Support / Helpdesk** — many professionals transition into security after 1-2 years of general IT support.
- **Junior Penetration Tester** — runs authorized tests against systems to find weaknesses.
- **Network Administrator** — manages the infrastructure that security teams depend on.
- **Security Auditor** — checks that policies, compliance, and controls are working.
- **Ethical Hacker Trainee** — an internship-style role that many consultancy firms offer.
Do not refuse a helpdesk or IT support role at the start. That experience teaches you the fundamentals that every security professional needs later.

### The Best Certifications for a Cybersecurity Career
Certifications are the fastest way to prove your knowledge to employers. For a beginner, the recommended order is:

- **CompTIA Security+** — the standard entry-level certification. It covers the core security concepts hiring managers expect.
- **CompTIA Network+** — excellent if you need to strengthen your networking fundamentals first.
- **Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH)** — a well-known offensive security certification for tool-based testing.
- **SSCP (Systems Security Certified Practitioner)** — a strong intermediate option.
- **OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional)** — the difficult, highly respected practical exam for serious pentesters.
- **ISC2 CC / CISSP** — start with the Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) and work toward CISSP after experience.
Vendor certifications also matter. For example, professionals working with Linux and automation platforms find the [Red Hat Certified System Engineer](/why-become-red-hat-certified-system-engineer/) path valuable, while those focused on networking often pursue the [Cisco](https://itsecuritynepal.com) roadmap. Choose certifications based on the job market in your region.

### How to Start a Cybersecurity Career: Step-by-Step
Follow these steps in order, and you will have a realistic, structured plan rather than an endless to-do list.

#### Step 1: Choose one starting point
Decide between offensive, defensive, or generalist. For most beginners, defensive security (SOC analyst) is the most accessible. Do not collect courses. Pick one track and finish it.

#### Step 2: Learn the fundamentals hands-on
Complete a foundational networking course, set up a home lab with VirtualBox or VMware, and practice on free platforms such as TryHackMe or Hack The Box. Hands-on practice matters far more than watching videos.

#### Step 3: Earn your first certification
Book and pass CompTIA Security+ within your first year. A certification gives you credibility with recruiters and HR systems that screen resumes by keyword.

#### Step 4: Build a visible portfolio
Document your labs, write short write-ups of challenges you solved, and publish them on LinkedIn. Employers in cybersecurity care deeply about demonstrable skill.

#### Step 5: Apply for the entry role
Apply to SOC analyst, IT support, and network administrator positions. Tailor your resume to the exact keywords in each job description and be patient through the process.

#### Step 6: Specialize after experience
Once employed, choose a specialty that you enjoy, then pursue the matching advanced certification.

### Where a Cybersecurity Career Can Take You
After a few years, your cybersecurity career can branch into highly paid roles such as:

- **Security Engineer** — designs and builds secure systems.
- **Penetration Tester / Red Teamer** — simulates attacks to find weaknesses.
- **Incident Responder / Forensics Analyst** — investigates breaches and contains damage.
- **Cloud Security Architect** — secures AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud environments.
- **Security Manager / CISO** — leads teams and manages organizational risk at the executive level.
Each specialty has its own ladder, but the foundation you build now remains valuable forever.

### How to Start a Cybersecurity Career in Nepal
For readers in Nepal, the fundamentals are identical, but there are local advantages. A growing number of Nepali IT training academies offer structured courses such as Ethical Hacking, Red Hat, Cisco, and CompTIA programs. Internships at security consultancy firms, banks, and telecom providers are realistic entry points. Nepali professionals also succeed strongly in remote and freelance security work, since the job is location-independent. Combine local training with global certification, and you expand your opportunities dramatically.

### Common Mistakes Beginners Make
- Consuming endless tutorials instead of practicing.
- Skipping networking fundamentals to jump straight into hacking tools.
- Chasing too many certifications without hands-on skill.
- Ignoring soft skills and report writing.
- Waiting for a perfect job while refusing an IT support starter role.
- Neglecting to document labs and build a public portfolio.
### FAQ
- **Can I start a cybersecurity career without a degree?** Yes. Practical skills and certifications often matter more than a formal degree in this field.
- **How long does it take to become a SOC analyst?** With consistent study, most motivated beginners reach the first job within 12-18 months.
- **Is cybersecurity a good career for the future?** It is among the most future-proof careers because threats and regulations continue to grow every year.
- **Which certification should I start with?** CompTIA Security+ is the recommended entry point for newcomers.
- **Can I work in cybersecurity from Nepal?** Yes, both locally and remotely. Many global companies hire Nepali security professionals.
### Conclusion
Starting a cybersecurity career in 2026 is challenging but very achievable. Focus on fundamentals, earn a recognized entry certification, build hands-on labs, and document everything you learn. The demand for qualified security professionals is not slowing down, so every step you take today brings you closer to a stable and rewarding future in IT security.
